claims.text: A trade union is an organisation of workers, joined and funded by them, that aims to protect and improve its members' pay and working conditions.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: Membership of a trade union is normally voluntary: members pay a subscription to fund it, and the union speaks for them as one body rather than each worker bargaining alone.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: A trade union is an organisation of workers that bargains with employers over pay and conditions; it is not trade between nations, and not a body that promotes a country's trade.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: Collective bargaining is negotiation between a trade union and an employer over the pay and working conditions of the union's members, with the union speaking for all of them as one body.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: The main roles of a trade union are negotiating pay and conditions through collective bargaining, protecting members' rights at work, representing members in disputes with the employer, and pressing for safer workplaces and training.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: Because a union negotiates for many members at once, an individual member tends to carry more weight in a wage negotiation than a worker speaking alone, provided the union's members make up a large share of the workplace.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: A union's role in the economy is discussed at the level of the whole labour market - wages and conditions across many workplaces - while a question about firms asks for effects inside particular employers, such as a higher pay bill.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: Where a union secures higher pay and clearer conditions, workers' income and job satisfaction tend to rise, staff turnover tends to fall, and the firm may spend less on recruiting and training replacements.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: A wage rise won by a union raises a firm's pay bill, so the firm may raise prices or shrink its workforce by not replacing workers who leave, particularly when its buyers can switch to cheaper imports.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: Industrial action such as a strike stops production while it lasts, so the firm loses output and the striking workers lose pay for the days they are out.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: Whether trade union activity helps or harms depends on conditions: whether pay rises match output per worker, whether the economy is creating jobs, and whether the union and the employer bargain or fight.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.
